html:
The Pantokrator Monastery is a large Byzantine monastery in Constantinople, built between about 1118 and 1136 by Emperor John II Komnenos and his wife Irene of Hungary. It is now the Zeyrek Mosque in Istanbul, above the Golden Horn.

It was dedicated to Christ Pantokrator, "ruler of all". The complex had three churches side by side, one of them a funeral chapel where emperors of the Komnenos and later the Palaiologos families were buried, among them John II and Manuel I. Its founding charter survives. It describes a hospital of 50 beds in wards for different illnesses, with doctors on duty, including a woman doctor for the women's ward, and a home for the old.

After the sack of 1204 the Venetians used it as their base. After the Ottoman conquest it became a mosque. After Hagia Sophia, it is the largest Byzantine church building still standing in the city.
sum: The Pantokrator Monastery is a large Byzantine monastery in Constantinople, built between about 1118 and 1136 by Emperor John II Komnenos and his wife Irene of Hungary. It is now the Zeyrek Mosque in Istanbul, above the Golden Horn.
